There's no reason to continue using discs. They're slow compared to other similarly cheap options, the worst of that is the seeking and spin-up times. With games getting huge, it doesn't make sense. I'll just make a bulleted list:

  • Faster - solid state (whether SD-based or more like a SSD) is simply faster, especially for random reads.
  • More durable - assuming they don't make them in a super thin form factor.
  • Expandable - presumably the cartridge's storage is nearly unlimited, or it could be. Up to some maximum of like 2TB but that's plenty right now.
  • Flexible - They could do something like moving all game storage to the cartridge. I might not suggest you move game saves to it, but certainly game updates. Make sure only the console can write to the cartridge and download updates directly to that. They can make consoles cheaper at the cost of somewhat more expensive games, maybe. This is debatable.
  • Smaller - There's no situation where they will have to occupy the amount of space that a CD requires. Standard 2.5" SSDs up to 1TB are still smaller. There's a lot of design liberty that a cartridge would afford.

It just makes sense to go back to cartridges now that storage is cheap. If all the console makers moved to this model, it could drive down the price of solid state storage even lower.

She brags about her cholesterol being low, when it's total cholesterol, which is a combination of LDL and HDL. Overly simplified, you want your LDL to be low, and your HDL to be high. HDL is the "good" cholesterol that is improved by a healthy diet, especially one rich in nuts/fish/vegetables/healthy oils, and by exercise.

She posts about her total cholesterol being 118 mg/dl, but her risk ratio (total cholesterol divided by HDL) is 3.8. Risk ratio is used to accommodate for the importance of HDL. Your total cholesterol could be high, but if it's because your HDL is high, then it's not important. You will then have a low risk ratio.
